plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Gnarled branches covered in small, fragrant, five-petaled blossoms appear while the landscape is still bare and chilly. Their sweet, spicy scent drifts over frosty gardens and shrine grounds, and it is one of the first signs that spring is coming.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to March, with the earliest blossoms in the mildest regions opening in late January and early February
plants.location: Japan, especially the milder regions of western and southern Honshu and Kyushu
plants.funFact: Ume blooms weeks before cherry blossoms. In Japanese culture it is the flower that heralds spring, and the fruit is pickled to make umeboshi or steeped to make plum wine.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs carry rose-like flowers in a range of forms, from simple cups to full double blooms, against dark, leathery leaves. They bring bright color to the quiet winter garden.
plants.bloomingSeason: Different varieties flower from autumn into spring, with many at their peak in mid-winter, including February
plants.location: Gardens of the southeastern United States, Japan and mild temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Both belong to the same genus.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems rise above arching, strap-like leaves and carry round clusters of funnel-shaped blue flowers. They put on a showy summer display in warm gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mostly November to February in the southern hemisphere summer
plants.location: Southern Africa, and widely grown and naturalized in Australia
plants.funFact: Despite its common names, it is not a true lily. The name comes from Greek words meaning love flower.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Nodding, white, bell-shaped flowers with green-marked inner petals push up through cold soil, and sometimes through snow. They carpet woodlands, churchyards and hedge banks in drifts.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter, generally February to March, and sometimes earlier in mild seasons
plants.location: Woodlands and gardens across the United Kingdom and Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make a natural antifreeze-like protein that helps them survive frost. A compound in the bulbs, galantamine, has also been used in medicine.
